title: Aurora Reserve Operator Panel — Dedicated GPU Capacity Console
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a consolidated operator-facing panel for managing Dedicated GPU capacity (named 'Aurora Reserve Operator Panel'). The goal is to give platform teams and SREs a single surface to observe fleet health, adjust autoscale policies, apply short-term burst overrides, and preview cost/latency impact of changes before committing. This ticket captures the high-fidelity prototype, interaction spec for safe rollouts, and a compact emergency flow for on-call remediation.
design_notes: Primary personas: Platform Engineers, SREs responsible for Dedicated capacity and on-call rotations.
Top-level layout: left navigation for pools list + filters, central timeline with multi-layer signals (availability, queued jobs, thermal warnings), right rail for controls and quick actions.

New control concepts: 'Anchorboard' (safe knob set for reserve targets and burst windows), 'Predictive Slack' slider (estimates headroom and suggested burst capacity), and 'Cost-slice Preview' (3-hour, 24-hour, 7-day cost delta forecast based on current settings).

Autoscale policy composer: inline rule editor with human-friendly heuristics (latency SLA target, p95 token latency, backlog threshold) and test-run simulation button to view modeled outcomes over past 7 days.
Burst window UX: allow ephemeral bursts with automatic decay and canary group assignment. Burst requests must show estimated cost and fall back to lower-cost model variants if budget exceeded.
Safety: every adjustment requires a two-step confirmation for changes that increase reserve commit or uncap burst limits; ephemeral changes create a rollback marker visible in the rollout timeline.
Integrations: rollout hooks with Redwood's rollout engine to enqueue changes as canary -> ramp -> full. The panel surfaces rollout status and quick rollback buttons.
Accessibility: keyboard-first controls for the Anchorboard sliders and ARIA labels on timeline annotations.
Mobile: condensed view for on-call mobile notifications showing critical metrics and single-tap emergency throttle.
Tradeoffs discussed: showing both cost and latency projections increases cognitive load; we bias toward small multiples of the current baseline with clear defaults to reduce risky operations.
Engineering constraints: prototypes assume availability of per-pool telemetry and a simulation endpoint that can replay 7 days of events; fallbacks defined if simulation data is unavailable.

Open questions: how to represent cross-pool dependency when multiple pools share burst budget; whether to expose tenant-level throttles in the operator panel or in a separate 'tenant controls' surface.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype in Figma with annotated interactions for Anchorboard, Predictive Slack slider, and Cost-slice Preview.
Clickable prototype demonstrating the two-step commit flow and the emergency rollback interaction.
Design spec documenting API contracts to request simulation and to submit tentative rollout objects to the rollout service.
Usability test with at least 5 platform engineers showing they can: identify high-severity thermal events, configure a safe ephemeral burst, and preview cost impact within 5 minutes.
Handoff packet (assets + tokens + component list) delivered to frontend with accessible markup guidance and CSS tokens.
Edge-case flows documented (simulation unavailable, cost-estimate stale, rollback conflicts).
